title: PostgreSQL HA with Patroni, etcd, HAProxy and Mattermost

release.label: Enrolled learner release — clean baseline verified

steps.title: Identify a PostgreSQL role
steps.why: Stable roles prevent operating on an address or index that can change.
steps.expected: Observer binds this terminal to pg-ha-1 generation 1.
steps.hint: Use the terminal already targeted to pg-ha-1.

steps.title: See the three-member DCS
steps.why: Three voting members tolerate one member loss, not majority loss.
steps.expected: Exactly three started voting members and zero learners.
steps.hint: Use the certificate-bound private node address, not 127.0.0.1.

steps.title: Name the availability boundary
steps.why: PostgreSQL is HA; HAProxy and Mattermost are deliberate single points in this profile.
steps.expected: Writer frontend and Patroni /primary checks are observed.
steps.hint: Find the frontend, backend, and health path.

steps.title: Verify the pinned etcd artifact
steps.why: A production cluster begins from immutable, verified software rather than an unpinned download.
steps.expected: The node reports etcd 3.6.14 from the approved SUTA artifact set.
steps.hint: Read the first version line; do not download a replacement.

steps.title: Inspect the member certificate
steps.why: Each etcd member certificate must bind its stable role and current private address.
steps.expected: The certificate subject names dcs-1 and its SAN contains the current private address.
steps.hint: Compare the DNS role and IP SAN; never print the private key.

steps.title: Inspect the etcd systemd contract
steps.why: Unique member identity, TLS endpoints and the three-peer bootstrap contract live in the service unit.
steps.expected: The unit uses dcs-1, mutual TLS, unique data storage and the three-member initial cluster.
steps.hint: Find --name, client/peer URLs and both client-cert-auth flags.

steps.title: Validate etcd mutual TLS
steps.why: Patroni depends on an authenticated, quorum-backed DCS.
steps.expected: The endpoint commits a proposal successfully over TLS.
steps.hint: A loopback endpoint will fail SAN verification by design.

steps.title: Verify the PostgreSQL filesystem
steps.why: Data, WAL, backup and log paths need explicit ownership and recovery boundaries.
steps.expected: data, wal, backup and log directories exist under /opt/pgsql with PostgreSQL ownership.
steps.hint: All four contracted paths are required.

steps.title: Inspect the Patroni contract safely
steps.why: The cluster scope, DCS transport and PostgreSQL paths must agree without exposing generated passwords.
steps.command: sudo grep -E '^(scope:|namespace:|name:|  protocol:|  data_dir:|  bin_dir:|  pgpass:)' /etc/patroni/patroni.yml
steps.expected: The output shows the learner cluster scope, HTTPS etcd transport, /opt/pgsql/data, /opt/pgsql/bin and protected pgpass path.
steps.hint: Use the bounded grep; do not display the full file because it contains credentials.

steps.title: Verify replication and rewind policy
steps.why: Replica cloning, pg_rewind and SCRAM host rules determine whether a failed primary can return safely.
steps.expected: Rewind, slots, checksums and exact-node SCRAM rules are present.
steps.hint: Verify the safety controls without printing authentication values.

steps.title: Verify Patroni bootstrap
steps.why: The leader must be ready before replica candidates start their first clone.
steps.expected: One leader and two streaming replicas appear on one timeline.
steps.hint: Use the absolute patronictl path installed by the lab.

steps.title: Validate writer routing
steps.why: HAProxy must route only to Patroni's current primary.
steps.expected: Configuration is valid and every backend uses /primary health.
steps.hint: A TCP-open replica is not a valid writer.

steps.title: Inspect role-aware health checks
steps.why: A stable endpoint is safe only when backend eligibility comes from Patroni role truth.
steps.expected: HAProxy sends GET /primary on port 8008 and lists exactly three PostgreSQL backends.
steps.hint: Confirm both the REST path and all three role names.

steps.title: Verify the workload database route
steps.why: Mattermost must use the unchanged HAProxy writer endpoint rather than a PostgreSQL node address.
steps.expected: The redacted data source targets db-router-1 on port 5432 and reveals no password.
steps.hint: The command deliberately redacts credentials before display.

steps.title: Verify the application workload
steps.why: Database health alone does not prove application availability.
steps.expected: Mattermost returns status OK through its configured HAProxy database endpoint.
steps.hint: Use the node's private identity because the service is not public.

steps.title: Inspect streaming replication
steps.why: Two WAL senders prove both replicas are attached to the writer.
steps.command: sudo -u postgres /opt/pgsql/bin/psql -h /var/run/postgresql -Atc "select state,count(*) from pg_stat_replication group by state;"
steps.expected: The primary reports two streaming connections.
steps.hint: Run locally through the protected Unix socket.

steps.title: Verify data placement and checksums
steps.why: Correct storage and checksums are prerequisites for safe recovery.
steps.expected: PGDATA is /opt/pgsql/data and checksums are on.
steps.hint: Both output lines are required.

steps.title: Check Mattermost from the workload node
steps.why: The application is the end-to-end consumer of the HA database path.
steps.expected: The API reports status OK.
steps.hint: This is an application check, not merely a process check.

steps.title: Lose the primary process
steps.why: Prove election, fencing and unchanged writer routing.
steps.expected: A new leader is elected, the old primary is fenced, Mattermost writes continue, and redundancy is restored.
steps.hint: This approval-gated scenario is locked until its release canary passes.

steps.title: Lose one etcd member
steps.why: A three-member DCS must retain quorum after one member loss.
steps.expected: Quorum remains, Patroni stays safe, and the member rejoins uniquely.
steps.hint: Never test majority loss at the same time.

steps.title: Demonstrate the router SPOF
steps.why: The lab must distinguish database HA from application-path HA.
steps.expected: Database remains healthy while the application path fails, then returns after router recovery.
steps.hint: This is an honest boundary demonstration, not a PostgreSQL failover.

steps.title: Prove database topology
steps.why: Completion requires server truth, not a learner claim.
steps.expected: Exactly one leader and two zero-lag streaming replicas.
steps.hint: JSON output is evaluated structurally.

steps.title: Prove snapshot readiness
steps.why: Quorum without a recoverable snapshot is incomplete operations evidence.
steps.expected: The snapshot is readable and contains committed keys.
steps.hint: The lab stages the approved snapshot at this path.

steps.title: Review cleanup scope
steps.why: Temporary infrastructure is complete only when compute, storage, network and secrets have a bounded reset.
steps.expected: Eight roles, volumes, security group, certificates and secret references are enumerated without mutation.
steps.hint: This is a plan; actual reset remains approval-gated.

steps.title: Explain quorum loss
steps.why: A senior DBA must predict safe behavior before injecting a fault.
steps.expected: Answer distinguishes one-member tolerance from majority-loss write safety.
steps.hint: Explain what Patroni can and cannot decide without DCS quorum.

steps.title: Explain writer routing
steps.why: TCP health alone can route writes to the wrong PostgreSQL role.
steps.expected: Answer explains why HAProxy checks Patroni /primary.
steps.hint: Connect health, role truth and the stable endpoint.

steps.title: State the HA boundary
steps.why: Honest architecture separates database HA from router and application availability.
steps.expected: Answer names HAProxy and Mattermost as SPOFs in this profile.
steps.hint: Do not claim whole-system HA.
